definitions.gloss: to call in, to invite in
definitions.explanation: To summon someone to come inside or to a specific place.
To bring in customers, visitors, or attention through active promotion or appeal.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}に{友達|ともだち}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I called my friend into the room.

examples.japanese: {店員|てんいん}が{客|きゃく}を{店|みせ}の{中|なか}に{呼|よ}び{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: The store clerk is calling customers into the shop.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}が{次|つぎ}の{患者|かんじゃ}を{診察室|しんさつしつ}に{呼|よ}び{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The doctor called the next patient into the examination room.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}したので、{外|そと}で{遊|あそ}んでいた{子|こ}どもたちを{家|いえ}の{中|なか}に{呼|よ}び{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: It started to rain, so I called the children who were playing outside into the house.

examples.japanese: イベントで{多|おお}くの{観光客|かんこうきゃく}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To attract many tourists with an event.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいサービスで{若|わか}い{世代|せだい}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}みたい。
examples.english: We want to attract the younger generation with new services.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{自然|しぜん}を{生|い}かした{観光|かんこう}で{人|ひと}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}もうとしている。
examples.english: This area is trying to attract people through nature-based tourism.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{商業施設|しょうぎょうしせつ}ができて、{周辺|しゅうへん}の{店|みせ}にも{客|きゃく}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: A new commercial facility opened in front of the station, attracting customers to the surrounding shops as well.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE: {呼|よ}ぶ (to call) + {込|こ}む (into). The ～{込|こ}む suffix adds the meaning of drawing inward.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{客|きゃく}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}む (attract customers)
・{観光客|かんこうきゃく}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}む (attract tourists)
・{投資|とうし}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}む (attract investment)

Usage note: Often used in business contexts for marketing and sales activities. The related noun {呼|よ}び{込|こ}み refers to the act of soliciting customers on the street.
